facts.fact: A rolling torque reading of 12.43 on this pinion assembly was identified as way too low and therefore a failing result.
If the measured rolling torque is too low, the operator must increase the shim pack to raise the torque value.
facts.applies_when: rolling torque reading is below the required value

citation.transcript_quote: We have to increase our shims.

facts.fact: If the measured rolling torque is too high, the operator must reduce the shim pack to lower the torque value.
facts.applies_when: rolling torque reading is above the required value

citation.transcript_quote: If it's too high, reduce shims.

facts.fact: There is currently no fixed rule or standard that defines how much a given change in shim thickness will change the rolling torque value by a predictable amount.

citation.transcript_quote: as for the values and how we can decide what number of shim will increase by what torque, we don't know yet.

facts.fact: The shim pack is installed during Phase 7, which is the phase the operator must return to in order to adjust shims when rolling torque is out of range.
facts.applies_when: rolling torque result requires shim adjustment

citation.transcript_quote: Phase 7 is where we put the shims.

facts.fact: Achieving the correct rolling torque through shim pack adjustment is described by the operator as the hardest part of the pinion assembly process due to the absence of a defined standard.

citation.transcript_quote: The hardest part is getting the shim pack to have the right torque, standard is missing and adjusting it up and down is hard as there's no fixed rule.
